scenario: [LUNI.3.1] — `ns` and the three spellings of microsecond are time builtins accepted at duration positions. The suffixes appear at THREE different duration positions — schema `ttl`, pattern `within`, rule `cooldown` — because the builtin set is consulted per use site rather than once, so a table wired into one path and not another would still pass a single-position fixture. The three microsecond spellings are μs (U+03BC GREEK SMALL LETTER MU — the SI symbol, and the canonical form the label and diagnostics use), µs (U+00B5 MICRO SIGN, the Latin-1 duplicate most keyboards actually emit), and `us` (ASCII, for a keyboard offering neither). All three must resolve identically, and each has to be listed rather than normalised into the others: DS normalises identifiers to NFC, and NFC — unlike NFKC — does not fold U+00B5 to U+03BC.
rules_ds:
schema Pulse scope ttl 250_ns:
    v: Int

schema Blip scope ttl 3_μs:
    v: Int

schema Flick scope ttl 3_µs:
    v: Int

schema Twitch scope ttl 3_us:
    v: Int

schema Beat scope logical:
    v: Int key
    ts: Time

rule quick cooldown 500_ns:
    Beat within 750_ns
->
    log info "sub-microsecond durations"
